idiom_name: instance method composed of instance-method calls
implementation_notes: The Swift book notes that an instance method has implicit access to all other instance methods and properties of its type, so the coordinator is an ordinary instance method that calls its steps; value types make the pattern especially clean because each step operates on the same value and mutations are written back at the end. Members default to internal, so steps should be marked private explicitly, and steps that mutate a struct or enum must be mutating.
pitfalls: In a value type a step that mutates state must be declared mutating, and mutating steps cannot be called on a let instance - the compiler enforces what other languages leave to convention.
Default member visibility is internal, not private: forgetting the private keyword exposes every step to the whole module (and, with @testable import, to tests).
In classes, storing a step as a closure (self.reserveStock used as a function value) captures self strongly and can create a retain cycle if the same object holds the closure.
